annotations.name: System contract artifact regeneration: solc 0.8.14 to artifacts/v1 and v2

explanation.value:
System contract bytecode (governance v1 and v2, NativeCoinAdapter) is
produced by systemcontracts/compile. The tool downloads solc 0.8.14
to ~/.solc-bin if absent, invokes it on the Solidity sources under
systemcontracts/solidity/, and writes binaries to
systemcontracts/artifacts/v1 and artifacts/v2/. Those binaries are
go:embed'd into contracts.go and consumed at genesis time via
InjectContracts. The do-not-edit constraint on the artifacts (see
A10.codegen.no_edit_zones) is enforced by re-running this procedure,
not by static checks.

annotations.name: System contract lifecycle: Solidity source to genesis state and e2e tests

explanation.value:
System contracts travel a five-stage pipeline. (1) Solidity sources live
under systemcontracts/solidity/ (v1/, v2/, plus abstracts/, interfaces/,
libraries/, openzeppelin/ shared code and test/ contracts). (2) The Go
tool systemcontracts/compile invokes pinned solc 0.8.14 on them.
(3) Compiled bytecode lands in systemcontracts/artifacts/{v1,v2}/ as
hex-encoded files — codegen output, never hand-edited. (4) Native Go
loads the artifacts at process start: go:embed directives in
contracts.go populate SystemContractCodes; at genesis,
core.InjectContracts -> GetSystemContractsTransition turns them into
CodeParam/state entries so the chain database is initialized with the
contracts' code and storage. (5) systemcontracts/test/ exercises the
whole chain end to end (native + governance flows against a simulated
backend). Consequence for indexing/search: the shipped binary depends on
.sol sources through the embedded artifacts even though `go list` never
sees them — a build-graph-only view misses stages 1-3 and 5
(systemcontracts/test is outside the dependency graph, and the compile
tool is its own main). The knowledge dataset scope therefore adds them
explicitly (projects/stablenet/filelist.yaml: extra_packages
systemcontracts/test + systemcontracts/compile/..., extra_globs
systemcontracts/**/*.sol).

annotations.name: Transaction type taxonomy and txpool admission fork gates

explanation.value:
StableNet inherits geth's typed-transaction envelope and adds one
proprietary type. The full taxonomy (core/types/transaction.go) is:
LegacyTxType 0x00, AccessListTxType 0x01, DynamicFeeTxType 0x02,
BlobTxType 0x03, SetCodeTxType 0x04, and StableNet's
FeeDelegateDynamicFeeTxType 0x16 (decimal 22) for fee-delegated txs.

Pool admission runs through txpool.ValidateTransaction (core/txpool/
validation.go). After a per-pool capability check (opts.Accept bitmask)
and a size check, each non-legacy type is gated behind a fork
activation, in this source order: any non-legacy type requires Berlin;
DynamicFee additionally requires London; FeeDelegateDynamicFee requires
Applepie (StableNet's fee-delegation fork); Blob requires Cancun;
SetCode requires Anzeon (checked via AnzeonEnabled(), a global enable
rather than a block-number gate). A type whose fork is not yet active
is rejected with core.ErrTxTypeNotSupported before any signature or
state work.

After the common gas/fee/sender checks, fee-delegated txs get an extra
admission gate: types.RecoverFeePayer(chainID, tx) requires a declared
FeePayer (else types.ErrFeePayerNotSet), recovers the fee-payer signer
via FeePayer(NewFeeDelegateSigner(chainID), tx), and rejects with
types.ErrInvalidFeePayer when recovery fails or the recovered address
does not equal the declared FeePayer. This is
the stateless half; the stateful fee-payer balance check lives later in
ValidateTransactionWithState (ErrFeePayerInsufficientFunds).

annotations.name: Txpool mutation must serialize through the reorg loop

explanation.value:
The legacy txpool runs a single goroutine — `pool.loop()` (started at
core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:366 `go pool.loop()`) — that
owns the txpool's internal maps (pending/queue/all). All mutation
events (head change, new tx, reorg) are queued and applied INSIDE
that loop, which is why the txpool data structures are not
individually locked: the loop is the serializer.

The sealer (miner/) and the txpool reorg loop interact across this
boundary: when the sealer requests a payload, it observes the
txpool's state at a point AFTER a reorg-run; mutating txpool maps
directly from the sealer (or from a tx-submission handler) WITHOUT
going through the loop is a data race that can either lose pending
txs or double-include them.

The trap: an LLM adding a "fast path" that mutates pool.pending /
pool.queue / pool.all from outside the loop (e.g. inside an RPC
handler, or inside the sealer's payload-building hook). Symptoms are
intermittent: tx drops, double-spend rejection on a tx that was
validly removed, occasional miner crash on map iteration. Any new
txpool mutation MUST enqueue into the loop's channel, not call the
map mutators directly.

annotations.name: Epoch transition: how the next epoch's validator set is selected and pinned

explanation.value:
go-stablenet's validator set is fixed for the duration of an epoch
(10 blocks on Mainnet, 140 on Testnet). On the last block of each
epoch, the engine calls buildEpochInfo: it queries GovValidator
(system contract 0x1001) for the new candidate list and validator
indices, then writes an EpochInfo into that block's
Header.Extra.WBFTExtra.EpochInfo. From the next block onward,
GetValidators returns the new set; intra-epoch blocks omit
EpochInfo. Backend.GetValidatorsForVerifying provides the previous
epoch's set in parallel so cross-epoch block verification can match
signers against the correct validator set.
